note: Free Rein's pieces: the idealized harness as sections of pieces, how each piece is done on each core, and combos between pieces. Detection and combos are rules over the extracted graph, evaluated by core/src/judge/evaluate.ts, so nothing here can claim what the harness does not do. Per-core answers carry a confirmed flag: true = known, false = believed but not confirmed, null = no known way. Each answer is [how, status, source]: status true = confirmed, false = believed, null = no known way; source names an entry in that runtime's sources (model/runtimes/<id>.json), so every claim says how it is known. Type audit applied 2026-10-02.

slots.name: Instructions
slots.job: what it's told before it acts

items.name: Project instructions

tiers.name: Tuned
tiers.means: Under 200 lines, and every @import resolves within four hops

tiers.name: Enforced

items.name: Personal instructions

tiers.name: Equipped

tiers.name: Tuned

tiers.name: Enforced
tiers.means: Every rule in it about an action is backed by something the agent can't get around

items.name: Folder instructions

items.example: web/CLAUDE.md with the frontend's conventions

tiers.name: Equipped
tiers.means: A CLAUDE.md below the root, or rules in .claude/rules

tiers.name: Tuned
tiers.means: Each says where it applies (a rules file with paths:), stays under 200 lines, its imports resolve, and none contradicts the root CLAUDE.md

tiers.name: Enforced
tiers.means: Every rule in them about an action is backed by something the agent can't get around

items.name: Injected context

tiers.name: Tuned

rows.name: Always read

rows.name: Set routines

tiers.name: Enforced

tiers.name: Proven

items.name: Autonomous runs

slots.name: Guardrails

items.name: Permission rules
items.what: Allow or deny decided before the model even sees the request.
items.example: allow npm test, ask before git push

change.does: Adds allow and ask rules, for example allow tests to run, ask before git push.

tiers.name: Equipped
tiers.means: You have permission rules

tiers.name: Tuned
tiers.means: Every rule is specific: none allows a whole tool

tiers.name: Enforced
tiers.means: No high-stakes situation is left with nothing stopping it

tiers.name: Proven
tiers.means: Your rules have decided real actions in your recent sessions

items.name: Blocking hooks
items.what: A hook can refuse an action outright, not just ask.
items.example: a hook refuses an unreviewed write to decisions.md

change.does: A PreToolUse hook that refuses edits to the files you list as protected (exit 2), registered before every edit. Edit the list to change what it protects.

tiers.name: Equipped
tiers.means: A hook that can refuse an action

tiers.name: Tuned
tiers.means: Each one's script is there, and its matcher names what it's for rather than every tool

tiers.name: Enforced
tiers.means: A hook that can refuse sits in front of file writes and of commands

tiers.name: Proven
tiers.means: It would have refused real actions from your recent sessions

items.name: Sensitive data guard
items.what: Keys, private files and personal information can't be read or sent out.

tiers.means: Something keeps secret files out

tiers.name: Tuned

tiers.name: Enforced
tiers.means: It covers commands too: a Read rule doesn't stop `cat .env`, so the sandbox or a hook has to

tiers.name: Proven

items.name: Notifications

combos.name: Continuity
combos.effect: The next session picks up the work itself, not a retelling of it.

combos.name: Curated knowledge base
combos.effect: Nothing enters the knowledge base without your sign-off.

combos.name: Grounded recall
combos.effect: It finds and cites what it knows, instead of loading everything up front.

combos.name: Defense in depth
combos.effect: Routine checks happen automatically, and you only see what needs judgment.

combos.name: Knows when to stop
combos.effect: Work has a finish line a check enforces and a retry budget, so it neither quits early nor loops forever.

combos.name: Learning loop
combos.effect: What happened gets scored, and the scores feed back into the harness.

combos.name: Designed crew
combos.effect: Agents hand off in a planned shape, so their work can be followed and checked.

combos.name: Earned completion
combos.effect: Work only counts as done when the check against the written criteria passes.

combos.name: Approval fatigue
combos.effect: Every guard asks you, and nothing can refuse on its own. The model behaving well is doing all the work.
combos.lifts: Wire the blocking hooks onto real write paths.

combos.name: Heavy pack
combos.effect: {weight} lines of context are paid up front, every session, before any work starts.
combos.lifts: Add retrieval, or trim the instructions so each mode loads only its part.

combos.name: Unread record
combos.effect: Everything is written down and nothing is ever scored, so the record can't make the harness better.
combos.lifts: Add evals, or a regular review of the feedback it captures.

combos.name: Accidental swarm
combos.effect: Agents spawn agents with no planned shape, so nobody can follow who did what.
combos.lifts: Declare how the agents connect and hand off.

combos.name: Too many tools to choose from
combos.effect: With {skills} skills, the model picking one by reading every description gets unreliable.
combos.lifts: Narrow the choice before the main model picks: a decision model (see Modalities), or fewer, sharper skills.

combos.name: Marks its own work
combos.effect: The agent that did the work is the only one judging whether it's done.
combos.lifts: Add an independent checker, or a completion check that runs the tests.

combos.name: Closed loop
combos.effect: Done is written down before work starts, checked when it ends, and measured over time.

combos.name: Paper trail
combos.effect: Every session leaves a record and a receipt, and both reach your own monitoring.

combos.name: Safe autopilot
combos.effect: It can run unattended: something refuses, something contains, and something checks the result.

tiers.name: Guided
tiers.blurb: Protocols, a knowledge base, and a person who approves.

tiers.name: Gated
tiers.blurb: Checks that can refuse on their own, and a record of what happened.

tiers.name: Governed
tiers.blurb: Done is defined, quality is measured, every session leaves a receipt.

progression.note: XP for each step a piece matures (empty, started, equipped, hardened: cumulative), for each achievement earned and each weak spot cleared, and for each situation the harness covers (its own pieces decide it, rightly for the stakes; high stakes count more). Level n starts at level_curve × n² XP (rounded up), to max_level. Ranks are tiers by their game names (names and rules still open). A collection (skills) earns up to gap_xp more: a share for each item with no gaps, up to gap_items of them, so adding a weak item never lowers XP: hardening is a profile per item, not a level. A piece with tiers (Equipped, Tuned, Enforced, Proven) earns tier_xp in all, split evenly across its tiers.

trust.note: What people let an agent do, and the controls that would justify it. Evidence is each category's controls weighted by strength (asks 1, checks 2, blocks 3).
trust.judgement_note: A judgement call is work where asking you is worth it: what it knows, whether it's done, acting with no one there. Editing files and running commands are routine: a rule or a check can decide them, and asking you each time is babysitting.
